title: Near-atomic cryo-EM structures of small proteins without scaffolds

concept.text: Determine three-dimensional structures of small, unbound proteins by single-particle cryo-EM, below the roughly 50–70 kDa range where particles become too low in contrast to align. Proposed completion test: single-particle cryo-EM structures at 3 Å or finer (gold-standard FSC 0.143) of monomeric proteins of 20 kDa or less, with no fiducial scaffold, binder, fusion or symmetric assembly adding mass, reproduced on several unrelated targets and by an independent group. Test set by: no outside body sets it; the 3 Å and 20 kDa thresholds are editorial, near myoglobin (17 kDa), the target the laser phase plate developers name. Overlaps: CRX-01. Sources given: [UC Berkeley news, 11 June 2026](https://news.berkeley.edu/2026/06/11/a-breakthrough-in-electron-microscopy-delivers-sharper-images-of-our-bodys-tiniest-proteins/). Sources given: https://news.berkeley.edu/2026/06/11/a-breakthrough-in-electron-microscopy-delivers-sharper-images-of-our-bodys-tiniest-proteins/.

page.title: Near-atomic cryo-EM of small proteins without scaffolds
page.definition: Single-particle cryo-EM, which averages electron images of frozen molecules, yields a structure with a traceable backbone and resolved side chains for most amino acids in a monomer no larger than myoglobin, about 17 kilodaltons (kDa). No protein scaffold, binder, fusion or assembly adds alignment mass.

goal.need: Approximately 75% of proteins in the human proteome are below 50 kDa. Among EM-derived PDB structures deposited since 2015 with resolution better than 4 Å, 97% represent macromolecules above 50 kDa. Small particles scatter fewer electrons, weakening the signal used to determine their orientations. Determining their structures without added alignment proteins would extend direct cryo-EM measurements into this underrepresented mass range.

statements.body: University of California, Berkeley, Müller laboratory
statements.quote: 17 kilodaltons (the size of the protein myoglobin).
statements.context: The university's report of 11 June 2026 identifies this as Müller's target for the minimum protein mass accessible using the laser phase plate.
The academy's Nobel Prize scientific background summarizes Glaeser's theoretical estimate of the lower particle-size limit. This is a feasibility estimate.

completion.title: A scaffold-free monomer no larger than myoglobin yields a near-atomic cryo-EM structure.
completion.criterion: A peer-reviewed single-particle cryo-EM reconstruction of a monomer no larger than myoglobin, about 17 kDa, directly resolves the peptide backbone and side chains for most amino acids, supporting an atomic model. Alignment uses the target itself, without a protein scaffold, binder, fusion or mass-increasing assembly. Independently reconstructed half-maps establish resolution using Fourier shell correlation at 0.143. Approximately 3 Å is the field's guide to side-chain visibility, rather than an additional numerical pass condition.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of Müller's stated mass target and published single-particle cryo-EM interpretation and validation conventions.
completion.basis: Developer papers, academy material, EMDataBank validation guidance, and agency, roadmap and prize searches yielded no adopted combined test. This joins Müller's mass target to the field's side-chain criterion. His 19 October 2026 SLAC abstract reports sub-3 Å lysozyme at 14 kDa, but that abstract is not peer reviewed and supplies no particle count, half-map validation or explicit scaffold exclusion.

milestones.title: A scaffold-free monomer no larger than myoglobin yields distinct two-dimensional projection averages.
milestones.criterion: Particle images align into class averages, each representing a homogeneous group of molecular views, with distinguishable orientations of a monomer no larger than myoglobin, about 17 kDa. No added protein supplies alignment mass. A thesis accepted on 6 November 2018 reports classification of 140,540 myoglobin particle images and selection of about 40,000 particles from the best classes.
milestones.set_by: Single-particle cryo-EM community, as described in Cheng et al. (2015), section on 2D clustering. The convention applies at any mass; its application here uses the completion test's mass scope.
milestones.threshold_quote: alignment and grouping of the data into homogenous subsets.

milestones.title: A scaffold-free monomer no larger than myoglobin yields a map resolving secondary structure below 10 Å.
milestones.criterion: A three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction of a monomer no larger than myoglobin, about 17 kDa, resolves secondary structure, including rod-like α-helical densities where helices are present. Resolution better than 10 Å must be supported by the visible structural features. The myoglobin experiment documented in the thesis accepted on 6 November 2018 did not produce a converged three-dimensional reconstruction.
milestones.set_by: Single-particle cryo-EM community, as described in Skiniotis and Southworth (2016), section on 3D map interpretation. The structural criterion applies at any mass; the mass scope follows the completion test.
milestones.threshold_quote: better than 10 Å is needed to observe rod-like densities corresponding to α-helices

milestones.title: A scaffold-free monomer no larger than myoglobin yields a traceable peptide backbone at about 4 Å.
milestones.criterion: A three-dimensional reconstruction of a monomer no larger than myoglobin, about 17 kDa, supports tracing its peptide backbone directly through the experimental density. The field associates this interpretability with approximately 4 Å resolution. Related evidence published on 14 April 2026 is a 3.38 Å reconstruction of PLK1 kinase domain–onvansertib from 200,803 particles with β-octyl-glucoside. Its purified complex was approximately 37.9 kDa, with 31.6 kDa ordered mass, exceeding the target mass.
milestones.set_by: Single-particle cryo-EM community, as described in Skiniotis and Southworth (2016), section on 3D map interpretation. The structural criterion applies at any mass; the mass scope follows the completion test.

not_found: No supporting peer-reviewed paper or deposited single-particle map was found for the 14 kDa lysozyme reconstruction reported in Müller's SLAC abstract for 19 October 2026.

results.finding: Scaffold-free 17 kDa myoglobin yielded 2D class averages from 140,540 particle images; about 40,000 particles were selected from the best classes.
results.detail: Volta phase plate imaging used myoglobin alone, with no added protein alignment mass. High-resolution 3D reconstruction remained unsuccessful. The thesis states that these SPA results had been published in peer-reviewed journals; the thesis itself is not a journal paper.
results.quote:
140540 extracted particles with a box size of 64 pixels were subjected to 2D classification in 
Relion2 (Scheres, 2012b) . Around 40000  particles were selected from the best classes for further 
processing.
